description: Sudoku-Extreme: solve rate against inference flop per puzzle for the looped baselines of the main table, rescored from the main-table checkpoints at fixed grids of their inference settings. No retraining; no setting chosen on test.
puzzles: full-all rows 10,000-19,999 (FRM test 1,000 + first 9,000 of full-00; EqR first10k), official rows from data/full-test/index.json
conventions:
One row per (method, knob, setting, training seed): solved, n, solve rate, mean and 99th-percentile flop per puzzle, the knob
values, the checkpoint, the scoring script and its SHA-256, the source files. Rows marked table1 reproduce the setting
of the paper's main table and are read from the main-table score files. Each method keeps its own answer rule, exact-solve
criterion and flop convention (flop per network call or step x calls; a multiply-add is 2 flop):
- HRM, TRM: k ACT steps; flop = k x one eval ACT step (results/flop-counts.json; experiments/runs/trm/T1/*-flops.json).
- EqR: depth D, breadth B; answer = lowest convergence score (top1_conv) among the first B trajectories of the B64 pass
  (path noise as the main-table B128 point), or the single-trajectory pass (B = 1, noise 0.01, as the existing B1 scores);
  random initial latents (std 1) in both; flop = D x B x one network evaluation (experiments/runs/eqr/E1/bench.json).
- FRM: N + 1 network calls (Sudoku held_t with N iterations; Maze NFE = N + 1); flop = calls x one forward.
- GRAM, knob "act_steps x samples": majority vote over N sampled trajectories of k ACT steps (ties by mean
  sigmoid(q_halt)); flop = k x N x one eval ACT step (baselines/runs/gram/flops/sudoku.json). Sudoku-Extreme only.
- TRMP, knob "rollouts": best of the first K rollouts by terminal confidence; flop per puzzle = K x (embedding +
  readout) + realized steps of those K rollouts x (step + halting head) (results/flop-counts.json components).
  Knob "step_cap": 64 rollouts, each stopped at step c at the latest; a rollout still running at c answers there
  with confidence q at c (as best_of with steps = c); flop = 64 x (embedding + readout) + sum of min(steps, c) x (step +
  halting head).
- EBR, knob "depth x samples" or "tau x samples": the lowest energy among the first N sampled trajectories, each run D
  segments, or stopped at the first segment end with tangential gradient norm |grad_M E| < tau (at most 64 segments on
  Sudoku, 16 on mazes); flop = segments x (one segment, + one gradient measure under the tau rule) per trajectory, + N
  energy evaluations when N > 1 (baselines/runs/ebr/flops/<task>.json, baselines/ebr/report.py).
- TRMP-fast (the lattice model), knobs "budget" (steps per puzzle at 64 chains) and "chains" (at
  budget 1,000): each setting is its own run of the chain search (sweep/trmp_lattice_sweep.py); answer = the first chain
  on a solved board, a puzzle unsolved within the budget is wrong; flop per puzzle = a_K + b_K x steps run on the
  puzzle, a_K and b_K counted by FullCounter over the whole search with K chains (count-k<K>.json, already FC2).
  Sudoku-Extreme only; added only when every setting of the three seeds exists.
Operation counts: every per-unit cost above is the arithmetic-only count of
results/op-counts.json (baselines/flops/fc2_export.py; convention in baselines/flops/fullcount.py), which replaced the
FlopCounterMode matmul-only counts named above; the assembly (units x steps, calls, samples) is unchanged. TRMP adds
the counted noise arithmetic per continuing step and the input check; EqR the top1_conv selection over B; EBR on
Sudoku scales its precomputed per-setting flop by the segment's count ratio (measure and energy ratios agree to 3e-4).
Puzzles: Sudoku-Extreme full-all rows 10,000-19,999 (official rows from data/full-test/index.json); Maze-Unique
the 1,000 test mazes. Dimensions: p = puzzles, k = steps or rollouts, d = depths, b = trajectories.
